Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um we have about 40 minutes, wanted to run through the self-serve flow, free credits, and how you'd get to first call. I'm Avery from Redwood, and with me is Diego who'll talk infra/perf.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Thanks, Avery. Hi Diego. Quick context: Pioneer is building a chat summarization feature for enterprise docs. Our blocker is demoing something to a pilot customer in the next 3 weeks, so time-to-first-call is kinda urgent.
[00:34] Diego Martinez: gotcha. um so typically self-serve / PLG path works the fastest. we can provision free credits on sign-up, you can call our hosted API in minutes. if your needs are predictable throughput we can talk Dedicated later.
[00:50] Lina Gomez: just to be clear — when you say "call in minutes" what does that mean for a small engineering team? how much work to wire in?
[01:02] Avery Chen: good Q. Typical path: sign up, API key, SDK or curl, sample prompt templates. our quickstart guides have code snippets for node/python and a postman collection. TTFT (time-to-first-token/call) usually under an hour for basic flows. for production-ish setup with SSO and secrets it's more like days.
[01:25] Ethan Ross: I'm interested in the hosted vs dedicated trade-off. we want low latency for interactive features — what's the difference in latency & cost?
[01:37] Diego Martinez: so hosted (Redwood API) is our multi-tenant offering — lowest friction, auto-scaling. latency is generally low for small bursts but subject to multi-tenant tail latencies. Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools — more predictable p99 and throughput, lower cold-start variability, and private gives you network isolation and VPC peering. cost obviously goes up as you move to Dedicated/Private.
[02:01] Maya Patel: ok, do you have SLO numbers or benchmarks we can look at?
[02:06] Diego Martinez: yes, we'll share our performance profiles — rough numbers are in the docs but we'll also propose a short benchmark for your canonical request pattern. for short chat-style prompts p50 is typically sub 200ms on tuned models, p95 depends on seq length and concurrency, could be 450-700ms unless you move to ded.
[02:26] Lina Gomez: is there an easy way to simulate our payloads? we have long docs and often context windows are big.
[02:33] Avery Chen: we can run a pilot with your prompts, Diego can run a small bench. if you want private we can run the same using a private control plane or onprem package but that takes longer to set up.
[02:48] Ethan Ross: security is a big deal for our pilot customer — they require SOC2 and internal audit logs, plus SSO and KMS. can you confirm what Redwood offers?
[02:59] Diego Martinez: yes. we support SOC2 type II attestation, we have audit logs retention options, SSO via SAML/OKTA, RBAC at token level, and KMS/HSM integrations for key management. for Private we give you customer-managed KMS and stricter egress controls.
[03:20] Maya Patel: perfect. would you be able to share the SOC2 report and a data flow diagram?
[03:25] Avery Chen: yep we'll send the security pack — SOC2, ISO statements, dataflow, and a short FAQ on retention and deletion. I'll attach the quickstart link and a sample Postman collection.
[03:36] Lina Gomez: about free credits — how many and what limits?
[03:41] Avery Chen: we usually give initial credits that let you do 5-10k tokens worth of calls enough for prototyping. if you need more we can extend based on use case and timeline; credits are applied to the hosted API.
[03:53] Ethan Ross: can credits be used on Dedicated or Private?
[03:56] Avery Chen: credits for hosted only typically; for Dedicated we do committed capacity conversations or time-limited pilot credits with a handoff. Private onprem is usually under a licensing/support arrangement.
[04:09] Maya Patel: ok that helps. specific question: if we sign up and hit a quota, do we see explicit rate limit errors and is there graceful fallback?
[04:18] Diego Martinez: yes you'll get clear 429s, we provide headers for rate-limit remaining, and the SDK supports exponential backoff. for production you'd want bursting or dedicated routing to avoid 429s during spikes. also built-in fallback to model variants is possible.
[04:34] Lina Gomez: about SDKs — are there first-class client libs and examples for streaming? we do streaming for incremental summarization.
[04:41] Avery Chen: node/python SDKs support streaming responses and function-calls; streaming may vary per model. we'll include code samples in the quickstart.
[04:52] Maya Patel: curious on dataset privacy — do hosted calls ever get used for model training? we need contractual guarantees.
[04:59] Avery Chen: by default we do not use customer prompts for training, and we have contractual options. for Private you own the control plane and data never leaves your network. we'll include language and options in the security docs.
[05:12] Ethan Ross: timeline — you mentioned 1 hour TTFT for devs. realistically with our internal approvals and SSO setup, what are we looking at to have a demo-ready flow?
[05:23] Avery Chen: if you want a basic demo to show your pilot customer, you could be ready in a day if nobody blocks SSO — sign up, quickstart, wire keys. with SSO and KMS probably 3-7 business days. if you want Dedicated/private numbers or compliance sign-off that extends based on procurement.
[05:41] Lina Gomez: what's the onramp for billing/limits for PLG? do we get a project with separate keys per environment?
[05:47] Avery Chen: yes you get a project/organization model, you can create multiple API keys and set per-key limits. billing is usage-based; we have a console to inspect token-level cost and latency.
[05:59] Maya Patel: okay let's talk success criteria for a pilot — what are sensible metrics?
[06:04] Diego Martinez: for a pilot I'd propose: functional correctness (top 3 prompt sets), latency (p50/p95 targets for interactive flows), and cost per 1k tokens. also error rate and stability over a 24-72 hour window.
[06:18] Maya Patel: makes sense. our pilot stakeholder (the customer) would want p95 under 600ms ideally.
[06:25] Diego Martinez: that's feasible with a Dedicated or tuned hosted profile depending on model and token length. we'll scope a bench that mirrors your longest context.
[06:36] Lina Gomez: any legal/procurement gotchas? we sometimes see IP clauses we need to watch for.
[06:42] Avery Chen: legal will provide our standard terms; for enterprise pilots we can add addenda around data usage and IP where needed. I'll include a short checklist in the follow-up.
[06:54] Maya Patel: great. what would a minimal pilot look like from Redwood's side?
[06:58] Diego Martinez: minimal pilot: 1) exchange security docs, 2) you get hosted credits and project, 3) we run a 24-48 hour benchmark with your sample prompts, 4) review results, recommend hosted tuning or Dedicated. we can optionaly do a canary canary rollout for a small percentage of traffic.
[07:19] Ethan Ross: if we want benchmarking, will you need network access or just request logs and payloads?
[07:25] Diego Martinez: network access isn't required for hosted. for Private we'd need VPN/VPC peering. for hosted bench we ask for representative payloads and expected concurrency, then we run tests against our endpoints with your prompts.
[07:38] Lina Gomez: are there obvious integration pitfalls?
[07:41] Avery Chen: common ones: not pinning model versions (so regen differences), not caching long prefixes (which increases tokens), and underestimating concurrency — we'll include best practices in the quickstart.
[07:53] Maya Patel: ok sounds good. next-step recap?
[07:56] Avery Chen: recap: I'll send security pack + quickstart + Postman collection and initial credits. Diego will send a short benchmark plan. Maya you'll confirm pilot stakeholders and timeline. we'll aim to have pilot kickoff next week if approvals go through.
[08:12] Lina Gomez: timeline note — our compliance reviewer is out until Friday, so earliest 10/15 for sign-off.
[08:18] Avery Chen: that's fine, we'll time the follow-ups accordingly.
[08:22] Maya Patel: thanks all.
[08:23] Avery Chen: thanks, we'll follow up via email, we'll include links to the docs and propose a deep dive slot in case you want dedicated perf numbers.
[08:31] (call ends)
